AI agents do the first pass. The founder checks every result before you see it.

## The old rule: Cheap, fast and good. The old rule said pick two.

It held because people’s time was the whole cost: cheap meant rushed, fast meant expensive, good meant slow. AI agents changed the cost of the first pass. They do it in a fraction of the time, for a few dollars. What is left is a person checking the result, and that is the part we never skimp on. So the rule is broken, and you get all three.

![A Venn diagram of three overlapping circles, cheap, fast and good, split by a lightning-bolt crack, with the swerving atom at the center where all three meet.](https://clinamenco.com/img/cheap-fast-good-venn-diagram-pick-three.webp)

*~~Not pick two~~, but pick three*

- **Cheap: A fraction of an agency’s price.** Agents do the heavy lifting, so a job takes hours, not weeks. We are paid fairly for the checking and the craft, and you still pay about a quarter of the cheapest agency setup fee we found, an eighth at the founding price.
- **Fast: Days, not quarters.** A written Quick Check within one business day. A fix or a website working within 5 business days of access. Every job is timed from signed scope to working result.
- **Good: Checked by the founder, backed by money.** A written scope, every result checked by a person before you see it, 30 days of fixes, and your money back if a One Fix doesn’t do what its scope says.

## What we do: Three ways to take work off an owner’s plate

Each at a fixed price with a written scope, each checked by the founder before you see it.

### Automations: Hand one weekly chore to AI

Owner-run businesses lose hours every week to the same few chores. We hand one of them to AI, in the tools you already use, and it is working within 5 business days of access.

**$195** founding price per fix · standard $390

- **A text back to every missed call.** Callers you can’t pick up get a text back, so the lead doesn’t walk.
- **Quote drafts from a web form.** A form on your site becomes a draft estimate for you to check and send.
- **Inbox sorting with draft replies.** Mail sorted by what it needs, with a reply drafted for you to send or bin.
- **Appointment reminders.** Reminders go out before each booking, without anyone typing them.
- **A website assistant.** Answers the questions you answer every day, from your own FAQ only.
- **A thank-you after each job.** Every finished job gets a thank-you and a way to book the next one.

### Websites: A website that says what you do and how to book

One page, built for phones first: your name, services, prices, hours and a booking button, written to be found in local search. Live on your own domain within 5 business days. You own the domain and every file. There is no monthly fee: the only running cost is your domain, about $10 to $20 a year.

This site is one. So is [briandominguezvoice.com](https://briandominguezvoice.com/), an audiobook narrator’s site, and two demos for local shops are just below.

**$195** founding price · standard $390 · changes and new pages under Care

### Software: Software for the way you take money

**Canopy** is our checkout for market stalls and food trucks, in development: one screen on the vendor’s phone for every way a customer pays (card tap, phone wallets, Cash App, Venmo, PayPal, Zelle, SNAP and market tokens, and cash). Card and wallet payments land in the vendor’s own Square account, and Canopy never holds the money. Zelle, Venmo, tokens and cash go in the same ledger, so the day adds up in one place, and there is nothing for the customer to install. We are starting with farmers markets: markets and vendors who want to try it early, [write to us](mailto:hello@clinamenco.com). [See how Canopy works](https://clinamenco.com/products/canopy/).

**Custom software.** When a chore needs more than an automation, we build the tool: a small server, a web app your team installs on their phones, an iPhone app. Payments go through your own Square or Stripe account, so you keep your money and your processor.

**$990** founding price for a small build · standard $1,450 · larger work by written scope, same terms

## The math on one chore: Three hours a week is 150 hours a year.

At $40 an hour, that is $6,000 of your time. If one fix takes that chore off your plate, it pays for itself within the first month, at $195 founding or $390 after. Then the hours keep coming back, every week.

Fifty working weeks a year. Put in your own numbers.

- Hours a week on the chore: 3
- What your hour is worth, $: 40

**150 hours and $6,000 a year.** One Fix at $195 pays back in about 2 weeks; at $390, about 4.

## How it works: Three steps, one person accountable

1. **You book a Quick Check.** 30 minutes on your weekly chores. Within one business day, a one-page written list: 3 chores, each with a fixed price.
2. **We build it.** In the tools you already use, working within 5 business days of access, with a handover and a one-page “how it works”.
3. **The founder checks everything.** AI agents, run by [Irie](https://clinamenco.com/products/irie/), the founder’s own open-source platform, on Anthropic’s Claude, do the first pass. He checks every result before it reaches you. Then 30 days of fixes.

The claims we make are the ones we can keep: a fixed price, a written scope, a deadline, and money back. No invented reviews or results. No claims we can’t back. No pressure.

## The name: Why Clinamen

![Atoms fall in straight lines; one swerves a little and lands somewhere new.](https://clinamenco.com/img/clinamen-swerve-diagram.webp)

*Fig. 1 · a small lean, a different landing*

**clinamen** /klaɪˈneɪmən/ (kly-nay-men), *noun*, plural clinamina

Latin, from *clinare*, to lean.

1. **The swerve.** In Lucretius’ *De rerum natura*, written around 55 BC, atoms fall straight down through the void until one, at no fixed time or place, leans a little from its path. Without that swerve nothing would ever meet, and nature would never have made a thing.
2. **Us.** A tiny swerve, a huge impact: one chore handed off, and the whole week lands somewhere new. Small swerves for small businesses.

**Say it:** CLI ’n’ Amen. CLI is the command line, where our agents do their work. Amen: so be it.

## Your data: How we handle your data

Data privacy is the first worry most owners raise. Here is what we do.

**What access we ask for.** Only what one job needs. For a missed-call text back, that may be your phone line settings and nothing else. We ask for a test account or sample data first, where we can. We never ask for passwords by email. We use each tool’s own sharing or admin access, so you can remove it any time.

**Where your data is kept.** In your own tools, where possible. Anything we must hold while we work stays in access-controlled accounts that only the people on your job can get into. We never post client data in public or use it in our own marketing.

**Who sees it.** AI agents do the first pass on your job. Evan, the founder, checks every result before you see it.

**When we delete it.** When the work ends, we delete the copies of your data we hold, remove our access, and confirm it in writing.

**Regulated data.** Health records, privileged legal files and financial advice carry their own rules. We scope the safeguards in writing before any work starts.

Questions: [hello@clinamenco.com](mailto:hello@clinamenco.com)

No. We set each fix up in the tools you already use. When the job is something new, it’s yours: a website lives on your own domain, and payments go to your own Square or Stripe account.

Until Sunday 31 January 2027 or our first 10 paying clients, whichever comes first.

Clinamen is Lucretius’ word for the swerve: atoms fall straight down until one leans a little from its path, and that small lean changes where everything lands. CLI is the command line, where our agents do their work; Amen means so be it.

# Irie: every AI coding agent, side by side

> Irie is the free, open-source app our AI agents run in: coding agents from any supplier, on any model, side by side in one calm view, each in its own git worktree. Version 1.0 for Mac and Linux.

- Page: https://clinamenco.com/products/irie/
- Book a free Quick Check: https://calendly.com/clinamenco
- Email: hello@clinamenco.com
- Updated: 2026-11-10

Open source · free · version 1.0

## Irie

Every AI coding agent you have, side by side, in one calm view.

Irie runs coding agents from any supplier, on any model, in the cloud or on your own machine. Each one works on its own task in its own copy of your code, and one window shows what every agent is doing and which one needs you. It is what our own agents run in.

[Install Irie](https://irie-people.github.io/irie/install.html)

[See the code on GitHub](https://github.com/irie-people/irie)

Free under the Apache-2.0 license. For Mac and Linux. No account, no server, no telemetry.

![Irie’s Mac app. A sidebar lists three agents by project: two working, and one marked red because it asks which color the signup button should be. Its terminal fills the right side, showing the question.](https://clinamenco.com/img/irie-ai-coding-agents-mac-app.webp)

*Irie’s Mac app, filmed with stand-in agents that run no model*

## Who it’s for: Anyone who works with AI coding agents

Whether you run one agent or a dozen, on Claude or on a model on your own laptop.

- **Developers** · Hand the grind to agents working in parallel, and spend your hours on the parts only you can do.
- **Teams at work** · It runs on each person’s own machine with the AI provider you already use. Nothing goes to a server of ours: there isn’t one.
- **Small firms like ours** · Several jobs moving at once, each in its own lane, with a person checking every result.

## How it works: Type a task, watch the cards, answer when asked

1. **Type a task.** Say what you want done. Irie starts an agent on it in its own git worktree, so agents never trip over each other’s changes.
2. **Watch the cards.** Every agent gets a card: working, done, or red when it has a question. Answer it, and the agent goes back to work.
3. **Use the right model.** A fast local model for the small jobs, a strong cloud model for the hard ones, and a second opinion from another supplier before anything reaches you.
4. **Come back to it.** Close the window and the agents keep working. Every session’s context is kept in git, so any of it can be picked up again.

## Why people use it: More done, less spent, nothing hidden

- **Take back your time.** Agents work side by side, each on its own task. You review, decide, and do the parts only you can do.
- **Any agent, any supplier.** Claude Code, or any other agent that runs in a terminal. If a supplier raises prices or goes away, swap it out.
- **Less spent per task.** Each task goes to the cheapest model accurate enough for it, and a model on your own machine costs nothing per token.
- **Nothing sent on its own.** No server, no account, no telemetry. Your agents talk to their own providers, as they would without Irie, and its records stay in folders only you can open.
- **One calm view.** A sidebar of cards in place of a wall of terminals. Red means an agent needs you; everything else can wait.
- **Free, and yours to change.** Open source under Apache-2.0 and built from public documentation. Read every line, and change what you like.

## Get started: One line to install

Paste it into a terminal on a Mac or Linux. It downloads the latest release, checks it, and installs `irie`, and Irie.app on a Mac. Then `irie setup` checks what else Irie needs and asks before it installs anything.

[Install guide](https://irie-people.github.io/irie/install.html) · · [Your first session](https://irie-people.github.io/irie/first-session.html) · · [What Irie is, part by part](https://irie-people.github.io/irie/what-irie-is.html) · · [Roadmap](https://irie-people.github.io/irie/roadmap.html)

```
curl -fsSL https://irie-people.github.io/irie/install.sh | sh
```

# Canopy: one checkout for every way a customer pays

> Canopy, in development, puts every way a customer pays on one screen on a market vendor’s or food truck’s phone: card taps, Apple Pay, Cash App, Venmo, Zelle, SNAP tokens and cash, with one ledger at closing. Cards land in your own Square account.

- Page: https://clinamenco.com/products/canopy/
- Book a free Quick Check: https://calendly.com/clinamenco
- Email: hello@clinamenco.com
- Updated: 2026-11-10

In development · farmers markets first

## Canopy

One checkout for every way a customer pays.

For market stalls and food trucks. Card taps, Apple Pay and Google Pay, Cash App, Venmo, Zelle, SNAP and market tokens, and cash, all on one screen on your phone. At closing, the whole day adds up in one ledger.

[Try it early](mailto:hello@clinamenco.com?subject=Trying%20Canopy%20early)

[See how it works](https://clinamenco.com/products/canopy/#how)

Card and wallet payments land in your own Square account. Canopy never holds your money.

## Who it’s for: Made for selling outdoors

Where a sale takes a minute, the till is one phone, and the next customer might pay any of eight ways.

- **Farmers market vendors** · Take whatever your customers carry, and close the day without a shoebox of slips.
- **Food trucks** · A faster line when everyone can pay their way, with tips when you turn them on.
- **Market managers** · Every stall’s SNAP, Double Up and market-buck tokens counted by program, so turning them in adds up. A market account with one statement for every vendor is planned.

## How it works: Ring it up, take it any way, close the day

1. **Ring it up.** Tap items on your quick keys, or type the weight for produce sold by the pound. Tax is added at your market’s rate, and nothing SNAP pays for is taxed.
2. **They pay on their own phone.** The customer scans the code on your screen and pays by card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or Cash App Pay. No app to install, no account to make. Or take a card tap through the Square app.
3. **Or any other way.** For Zelle or Venmo, they see your handle, the amount and a memo code, and you tap “I see it”. Cash shows the change due. Tokens are counted by program. One sale can be split as many ways as it takes.
4. **Close the day.** Totals by how people paid, the cash you should have against the cash you counted, the tokens to turn in, and a spreadsheet for your bookkeeper.

## At closing: The whole day, in one place

Every payment carries a mark that says how sure you can be of it, so you know what to chase before you pack up.

- **Confirmed by Square** Cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Cash App Pay, checked with Square itself.
- **Confirmed by you** Zelle, checks, and Venmo or Cash App sent to your own handle, once you tap “I see it”.
- **Tokens** SNAP, Double Up and market-buck tokens, which the market pays back.
- **Counted** Cash, checked against what the day’s sales say you should have.

## Why vendors want it: Every sale, none of the juggling

- **Never turn a customer away.** Card, phone, app, token or cash: whatever they carry, you can take it, on one screen.
- **Your money, your account.** Card and wallet payments go straight to your own Square account. Canopy never holds or moves money, and card numbers never touch it.
- **No cut of your sales.** Canopy adds no fee to your payments on top of Square’s own card fees.
- **SNAP rules built in.** Your market keeps its EBT machine. Canopy counts the tokens and checks what they can buy: no SNAP for hot food, Double Up for produce only, and no cash change.
- **Two phones, one stall.** A helper’s phone joins by scanning a code, and both see every sale as it happens.
- **Receipts anyone can check.** A customer who pays by card or app gets a receipt as a code, signed so anyone can check it’s real.

## Where it stands: Working end to end, on its way to a first market

### Works today, in testing

A whole market day runs end to end with a stand-in for Square: ringing up, every way to pay, refunds, two phones, receipts and closing.

### Next

Square’s test environment, then a first farmers market with real vendors.

### Planned

Canopy’s own Tap to Pay on iPhone, card readers over Bluetooth, digital market tokens in place of paper, ordering from the line for food trucks, and Stripe for vendors without Square.

## Questions: What vendors ask first

**Does Canopy hold my money?** No. Card and wallet payments go straight to your own Square account. Zelle, Venmo, tokens and cash are written in Canopy’s ledger, but the money never passes through us.

**Do my customers need an app?** No. They scan the code on your screen with their phone’s camera and pay in the browser.

**Do I need a Square account?** For card and wallet payments, yes: you connect your own. Stripe, for vendors without Square, is planned.

**What phone do I need?** An iPhone, to start. Canopy installs from the browser to your home screen, with nothing to download from an app store.

**What will it cost?** The price isn’t set yet, and Canopy won’t take a cut of your sales. Markets and vendors who try it early help shape it.

# A social media tool that waits for your yes

> In early development at CLI ’n’ Amen co.: a social media tool that plans, drafts and posts to every channel you use from one place, and publishes nothing without your approval.

- Page: https://clinamenco.com/products/social/
- Book a free Quick Check: https://calendly.com/clinamenco
- Email: hello@clinamenco.com
- Updated: 2026-11-10

In early development

## Social media that waits for your yes

We’re building a tool that plans, drafts and posts to every channel you use, from one place. Its AI will suggest, and you decide: nothing is published, changed or deleted without your approval.

[Hear when it’s ready](mailto:hello@clinamenco.com?subject=The%20social%20media%20tool)

[See how it works](https://clinamenco.com/products/social/#how)

For owners who do their own posting, and for the people who post for them.

## How it works: Draft, approve, and it goes out on time

1. **Connect your accounts.** Instagram, Threads and more, each through the network’s own official connection. It never asks for your main password.
2. **Drafts land in one queue.** Write a post, or drop ready posts into a shared folder for it to pick up. Each draft waits for you, with a preview for every network.
3. **You say yes.** Approve a post to go now or at a set time. Change it after you approve it, and it waits for you again.
4. **It posts, and checks.** Each post goes out at its time and is checked once it’s live. If the time slips by, the post waits for you instead of going out late.

## Why it helps: Your posts, out on time, and never without you

- **Nothing goes out without your yes.** Every post is approved by a person, and every change is logged.
- **One queue for every channel.** Write once, with a version for each network, and see the week in one place.
- **On time, or not at all.** A post goes out in its window, or waits for you. A stale post never goes out on its own.
- **A note every morning.** What went out, what comes next, and what needs you, in one short note.
- **Brands and clients kept apart.** Each brand or client gets its own accounts, posts and settings, with roles for who drafts and who approves.
- **AI that asks first.** On the way: drafts from your own material, for you to approve. It will never post on its own.

## Where it stands: Early, and moving

### Works today, in testing

Posting to several networks after approval, scheduling, a shared drafts folder, the morning note, and a workspace for each brand with its own logins.

### Next

AI drafts from your own material, a weekly report on what worked, and more networks.

### Want in early?

Tell us what you post, where and how often. [Write to us](mailto:hello@clinamenco.com?subject=The%20social%20media%20tool), and we’ll tell you when it’s ready.
